strings.name: Daphne Koller
strings.summary: Born in Israel and trained at Hebrew University and Stanford, Koller researched probabilistic graphical models and machine learning at Stanford. She cofounded Coursera with Andrew Ng to broaden access to university courses, then moved into computational biology and founded insitro for drug discovery. Her career connects algorithms, education platforms and biotechnology. Drug research goals still require experimental and clinical testing and should not be confused with completed treatments.

strings.influence.rationale: Advanced probabilistic machine learning, cofounded Coursera and developed AI-driven drug research, connecting scientific research with wider educational access.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Hebrew University of Jerusalem bachelor’s (1985) and master’s (1986); Stanford computer science doctorate (1993).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Probabilistic modeling
strings.highlights.h1.text: Studied uncertainty representation and learning from data, applying probabilistic models to biological science.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research and education ventures
strings.highlights.h2.text: Cofounded Coursera and founded insitro, extending computing research into online education and drug discovery.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Elected to the National Academy of Sciences
strings.timeline.t1.text: Elected after sustained machine-learning and interdisciplinary research, reflecting peer recognition.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Founding insitro
strings.timeline.t2.text: Established a drug research company combining machine learning and experimental biology.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joining Calico
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became chief computing officer, applying machine learning to biological data and health research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Cofounding Coursera
strings.timeline.t4.text: Established the online course platform with Andrew Ng to broaden access to university teaching.
strings.timeline.t5.title: MacArthur Fellowship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Received support for research in probabilistic reasoning, graphical models and learning.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining Stanford’s faculty
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began teaching and machine-learning research after postdoctoral work at Berkeley.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earning a Stanford doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed a computer science doctorate, then undertook postdoctoral research at Berkeley.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing a Hebrew University master’s
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a master’s after the 1985 bachelor’s, building foundations for computing research.
